note: Stage-task rules for plantain. Soil-moisture and temperature cut-offs are NOT included until each has a source (Sprint 1). Rules marked 'citation pending' come from the team's farmer-task list (26 Nov 2026) and must be sourced or changed to REFER before the test set is opened. 'Socket' = sucker used as planting material. Lower priority number = handled first.

rules.message: No rain was reported this week. If the rains fail, water the plantain. A sourced soil-moisture cut-off is not yet available, so check the soil and ask your extension officer if unsure.
rules.source: FAO crop information: Banana (frequent water supply; water deficit affects growth and fruit filling); cut-off pending

rules.concern: root system may need water during socket replacement
rules.message: No rain was reported this week. Make sure the root system of the plantain stand and the new sockets are watered.
rules.source: FAO crop information: Banana (frequent water supply); cut-off pending

rules.concern: possible banana weevil damage at the base
rules.message: Possible weevil damage at the base. Keep the farm clean, dispose of old plant residue properly and trap weevils with split pseudostems. Ask your extension officer if damage spreads.
rules.source: Nkakwa et al. (2007), Ghana J. Agric. Sci. 40, p. 182

rules.message: Importing sockets may be subject to import and plant-health rules. Please ask your extension officer before you bring sockets in.
rules.source: No source yet; safeguard rule, citation pending

rules.message: Support the plantain that are bending over with firm props so they do not topple or snap.
rules.source: Nkakwa et al. (2007), Ghana J. Agric. Sci. 40, p. 182 (firm props)

rules.message: Control the weeds. Cleared weeds can be left to decay on the field as organic matter.
rules.source: Nkakwa et al. (2007), Ghana J. Agric. Sci. 40, p. 178

rules.message: Place humus (organic matter) around the plantain stools.
Make the holes for the sockets.
Plant the sockets. Use clean, healthy sockets with the outer layer pared off.
rules.source: Nkakwa et al. (2007), Ghana J. Agric. Sci. 40, pp. 178, 182

rules.message: Flowering has started. Keep monitoring the flowers and the bunch.
Harvest the matured plantain. If you are unsure the bunch is mature, ask your extension officer.
Cut down the stalk of the harvested plantain and dispose of the residue properly.
rules.source: Nkakwa et al. (2007), Ghana J. Agric. Sci. 40, p. 182 (dispose of post-harvest residue)

rules.message: Propagate the sockets. Keep one or two to carry the next crop and remove the extra ones.
rules.source: FAO crop information: Banana (suckers removed except one or two for the ratoon crop)

rules.message: Harvest the sockets that are ready, for planting or replanting.
The reported sign can have several causes and no supported rule covers it yet. Please ask your extension officer to look at the crop.
rules.source: Safeguard rule: refer unexplained signs to an extension officer

rules.message: No concern matched the reported observations. Keep monitoring the crop and report again if conditions change.
